slides.title: A classifier needs a window of history
slides.lead: One instantaneous sample cannot describe a whole gesture.
points: The newest nominal 2 s becomes 100 × 6 values
SDK buffering resamples timestamps onto a 50 Hz grid
The first decision waits for a full window
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Keep preprocessing identical
slides.lead: Training and inference must agree on channel order, units and scale.
points: Convert accelerations to g and gyros to units of 4 rad/s
Clip to ±4; keep gravity instead of subtracting each window’s mean
Fixed scaling preserves how hard a motion is
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: A small 1D CNN learns temporal patterns
slides.lead: Convolution applies short learned filters along the time axis.
points: Early filters respond to local changes across channels
Later layers combine patterns into class scores
The lab guide describes about 1,800 parameters
The model receives the time series; the FFT is an analysis aid
slides.notes: Use shake stripes and the lift dip in the heatmap as intuition. Do not claim a particular learned filter without inspecting trained weights.

slides.title: Synthetic accuracy answers a narrow question
slides.lead: A high score on generated gestures does not measure real-world reliability.
points: Synthetic training tests the software pipeline
Different people, mounting, speed and sensor noise create a domain gap
Evaluate held-out people/sessions, not only more takes from the same person
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Collect and train with real motion
slides.lead: Each take contains 100 rows × 6 channels plus timestamps.
points: Press Enter, perform the gesture for 2 s, repeat
Use several people and independent sessions
The collector retries takes with too many missing samples
With one person, the trainer warns and splits per gesture
slides.code:
robotos-kws collect-imu --person yourname --takes 10
robotos-kws train-imu --data imu_dataset --out imu_artifacts
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Why an int8 model?
slides.lead: Quantisation reduces storage and arithmetic precision.
points: model_int8.tflite uses 8-bit values and is about 10 KB per lab guide
Scale and zero-point map quantised tensors to numerical values
A smaller model can suit an MCU; these labs still run it on the host
Do not convert model inputs to int8 by a plain cast
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Give the detector every sample
slides.lead: push updates the history and triggers inference when ready.
points: Default hop=200 ms: about ten new samples per inference
Default smoothing averages up to three probability vectors
Default refractory interval=1000 ms suppresses rapid repeated hits
These defaults were checked in the SDK source
slides.code:
det = rk.GestureDetector(str(MODEL), threshold=0.7, verbose=False)
det.push(s.t, s.accel, s.gyro)
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Read the probability bars
slides.lead: These are illustrative scores, not outputs of a loaded neural network.
points: Choose a preset or adjust the scores; values are normalised to sum to 1
The lab highlights the overall top class only if non-idle and above threshold
A confident idle class blocks a weaker gesture class
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Threshold creates a decision rule
slides.lead: Overall argmax → reject idle → compare score ≥ threshold.
points: Do not choose the best non-idle class after ignoring a larger idle score
Bar highlight is a score condition
Actual detection counters also obey smoothing, warm-up and refractory timing
slides.notes: Try idle=0.55, shake=0.30 with threshold=0.25. The result must remain no gesture because idle wins overall.

slides.title: Tap to tune the threshold
slides.lead: Lab 9.5 maps only the bar plot area to [0,1].
points: Top=1.0; bottom approaches 0.0
Only TOUCH_DOWN inside the plot updates the threshold
The emulator supports pointer taps and a keyboard-accessible slider
slides.code:
if t.event == TOUCH_DOWN and BAR_X <= t.x < BAR_X + BAR_W and BAR_Y <= t.y < BAR_Y + PLOT_H:
    det.threshold = round(1.0 - (t.y - BAR_Y) / PLOT_H, 2)
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Counts and probabilities answer different questions
slides.lead: A bar shows the latest smoothed score; a counter records accepted events.
points: A high bar need not increment on every redraw
The refractory interval separates repeated hits
Repeated gestures can still trigger again after cooldown
Label time-window metrics separately from event-level detection metrics
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Build a confusion matrix from labelled trials
slides.lead: Move the threshold and recompute predictions for the same fixed examples.
points: TP: gesture accepted on a positive trial
FP: accepted on a negative trial; FN: rejected positive; TN: rejected negative
This binary demo uses invented labelled scores, not measured lab accuracy
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Precision and recall expose different errors
points: Accuracy=(TP+TN)/all trials
At a stricter threshold, accepted trials shrink; recall cannot increase here
Precision need not improve monotonically on every dataset
An undefined ratio is shown as n/a, not a perfect score
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Run Lab 9.5 and compare sources
slides.lead: Use the same threshold on synthetic replay and real motion.
points: Check that imu_artifacts/model_int8.tflite exists
Tap MODEL on the board; tap high and low on its bars
If shake repeatedly becomes circle, investigate training-data mismatch
Choose thresholds from labelled evidence and application costs
slides.notes: Do not recommend an emergency-stop threshold from this demo alone. Ask which failure costs more and what independent validation would be needed.
